name: FlorentineEscape
source:
Prologue 
 
 Firenze, Italia – Nov. 8th, 1494 
 
 She struggled to quicken her pace without drawing the attention of the city guard. A woman of her status was well known and observed; easily identified by anything more than a passing glance. Alfonsina Orsino had tucked her flaxen-colored hair beneath a frayed veil in hopes of distorting her appearance, but her skin was too pale; her posture too upright to pass off as a peasant. The drab gown borrowed from her handmaiden was lighter than the gold embroidered layerings she was used to, but in this moment she was grateful. Though the sweltering heat of the summer had long since cooled, in her haste the rising sun still brought sweat upon her brow. 
 
 As Alfonsina turned the corner into the bustling Piazza della Signoria, she held her breath deep within her chest. Though the noise came from directly in front of her, the deep toll of the bell tower shook the ground and reverberated from every direction. A flock of pigeons, startled from the rumbling, abandoned their nests atop the Torre d ’ Arnolfo. The chime, echoing throughout the city, summoned the citizens of Florence to the steps of the Palazzo Vecchio, the seat of government. 
 
 Men and women alike filtered into the square carrying weapons and yelling obscenities. Alfonsina scanned the crowd warily for a familiar face, but saw only cold hatred in the foreign eyes of the common people. Too long had they endured the extravagance of the Medici family as children starved in the streets; too long had they entrusted loyalty in a coward who had sold out their territories and their freedom to the invading French. They did not want Piero ’ s arrogant promises or semantics; they wanted Medici blood.
retelling:
Narrating from Alfonsina Orsino's Perspective:

On a chilly November morning, Florence, 1494, I, Alfonsina Orsino, found myself cloaked in anonymity, swaddled in the folds of a drab gown that contrasted starkly with my usual attire adorned with golden embroidery. With furtive steps and downcast eyes, I darted through the labyrinthine city streets, desperate to evade recognition. The clamor of the bustling crowd served as an ominous soundtrack to my covert journey, a stark reminder of the tumultuous times that had gripped our beloved Florence.

The air was heavy with tension and unspoken fears, as if each breath I took was laden with the weight of the city's collective sorrow and anger. The streets teemed with armed men, their eyes gleaming with a fervor born of desperation and injustice. Their hatred for the Medici family, our ruling dynasty, seethed beneath the surface, threatening to erupt at any moment like a cauldron boiling over.

As I approached Piazza della Signoria, my heart pounded in my chest like a drumbeat that echoed the rhythm of my thoughts - fear, anticipation, and the unmistakable thrill of danger. The square was abuzz with activity, the cobblestones reverberating beneath the footsteps of the angry mob that gathered at the very steps of Palazzo Vecchio.

The bell from Torre d'Arnolfo tolled, its mournful peal piercing the cacophony of voices raised in anger and defiance. The crowd surged forward, their weapons glinting menacingly in the fading sunlight as they converged upon the seat of our government.

I stood, frozen in place, my breath hitching in my throat as I bore witness to this uprising that threatened to shatter the very foundations of our city. My heart ached for Florence, for the people who suffered under the yoke of the Medici's rule, and for my own family whose fate hung precariously in the balance.

But amidst the chaos and uncertainty, I felt a flicker of hope. A spark that ignited within me the belief that change was possible, that we could rise from the ashes of our suffering and forge a new path for ourselves. It was a fragile, tenuous hope, but it was enough to give me the courage to continue my journey, whatever destiny awaited me on the other side of the conflict that threatened to engulf our city.
